newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia FinMin submits 38 trln peso budget bill.
newsitem.headline: Colombia FinMin submits 38 trln peso budget bill.

text.p: Colombia's Finance Ministry submitted to Congress Tuesday its draft general budget of 38 trillion pesos, including debt servicing, for 1998 -- a 24 percent nominal increase compared to 1997.
The total budget, excluding debt servicing is 25.9 trillion, down from the 29.9 trillion pesos announced earlier this month, but 12 percent higher in nominal terms than this year.

The draft budget legislation, which Congress must now debate and approve before it becomes law, allows for 11 trillion pesos in debt servicing in 1998, compared with 7.4 trillion pesos this year. At least 2.6 trillion pesos of that will be spent servicing foreign debt -- up 23.7 percent on this year, the document said.

The budget document, with a foreword by President Ernesto Samper, sets out the governemnt's inflation target of 16 percent for 1998, compared with 18 percent this year. It also sets a 13.8 percent nominal devaluation target for the peso in 1998 against a 15 percent nominal devaluation target this year.

The draft bill reiterates previous Finance Ministry comments that the gross domestic product (GDP) growth target next year is 4.5 percent compared with this year's three percent, which was revised down.
The inflation and devaluation targets must still be officially approved by the central bank.
